title: Sudan Khartoum floods — Aug 2019
brief_outcome_free: Khartoum and the Nile / Blue Nile confluence, heavy seasonal rains and high river levels (Aug-Sep 2019). Riverine and urban neighbourhoods exposed to flooding and house collapse. You are the DOC duty analyst as the forecast window opens.

act1_quiz.prompt: It is August in Khartoum, at the Blue Nile / White Nile confluence. The kiremt season on the Ethiopian Plateau has been running above average. Why does rain falling hundreds of kilometres upstream matter for the duty analyst here?
act1_quiz.hint: The Blue Nile's flood wave is generated outside Sudan.
options: Above-average kiremt rain on the Ethiopian Plateau swells the Blue Nile and Atbara, so river levels at Khartoum can keep rising even on locally dry days
Upstream rain is irrelevant because rivers lose all their water before reaching Khartoum
Only rainfall inside Khartoum state can affect the Nile's level
Upstream rain lowers the river by recharging aquifers
act1_quiz.correct: Above-average kiremt rain on the Ethiopian Plateau swells the Blue Nile and Atbara, so river levels at Khartoum can keep rising even on locally dry days
act1_quiz.answer_note: Most of the Blue Nile's flood season flow is generated by June-September kiremt rainfall over the Ethiopian highlands and arrives at Khartoum days to weeks later. A persistently wet upstream season therefore loads the river toward high stages at the confluence regardless of the local sky, and dam operations upstream can add further pulses.
act1_quiz.bn_purpose: Why antecedent and upstream-catchment evidence keeps the riverine risk elevated even when the local forecast looks moderate.

act1_quiz.prompt: Beyond the rivers themselves, which exposure characteristic makes Khartoum's neighbourhoods vulnerable during a heavy-rain spell?
act1_quiz.hint: Think about what sustained rain does to traditional building materials on flat clay plains.
options: Widespread mud-brick housing weakens when saturated, and low-lying districts near the confluence flood from both river rise and poorly drained local downpours
Housing is uniformly reinforced concrete on elevated ground
Only riverside farmland is exposed; residential areas are out of reach
The city's storm drainage is designed for far larger events than any forecast
act1_quiz.correct: Widespread mud-brick housing weakens when saturated, and low-lying districts near the confluence flood from both river rise and poorly drained local downpours
act1_quiz.answer_note: Much of greater Khartoum, including districts like Omdurman, Sharq el Nile and Tuti Island at the confluence, is built of mud-brick on flat clay plains that drain poorly. Sustained rain saturates walls and roofs while ponding water and rising rivers attack the same low-lying neighbourhoods from two directions.
act1_quiz.bn_purpose: Exposure context: combined riverine and pluvial pathways mean moderate evidence on either channel still implies significant risk to housing.

decision.checkpoint_prompt: The ensemble mean may look benign but the tail signal is rising ahead of onset. What DOC level do you set, and why? A 'Watch + re-check + note the tail uncertainty' is a strong answer.

counterfactual.prompt: What if a precautionary no-regret action (alert Nile-corridor focal points, pre-position relief and ready evacuation) were taken at the lead round on the tail signal?
counterfactual.narrative: Acting on a short-lead tail signal is exactly what the flood BN's tail_risk node exists to surface. The counterfactual illustrates loss reduction without claiming certainty.
